definitive_patches.new: וּבַחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ מִֽקְרָא־קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כָּל־מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֲבֹדָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ י֥וֹם תְּרוּעָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶֽם: וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם עֹלָ֜ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֙חַ֙
definitive_patches.specific_evidence: Compared with the actual s254 crops. Upper marks: a curl over the ḥet of וּבַחֹ֨דֶשׁ, a geresh stroke over the ʿayin of הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י, revia over the ḥet of לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ, two upper marks on קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ (one over qof, one over shin), zaqef over the kaf of לָכֶ֔ם, a curl over the tav of וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם, geresh over the lamed of עֹלָ֜ה, two upper marks on נִיחֹ֙חַ֙. Lower marks: meteg under the mem of מִֽקְרָא, the etnaḥta wedge plus meteg in תַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ, silluq in לָכֶֽם:, the angled mahpakh under the resh of לְרֵ֤יחַ. Every conjunctive (munaḥ, merkha, tipḥa) has a mark in the right lower position. Their shapes are only partly crisp at this size, but nothing contradicts them. This replaces the independent-274 note that no s254 crops were supplied: the s254 crops do exist and were compared.

definitive_patches.new: פַּ֣ר בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר אֶחָ֖ד אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֑ד כְּבָשִׂ֧ים בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֛ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה תְּמִימִֽם:
definitive_patches.specific_evidence: A clear etnaḥta wedge under the ḥet of the second אֶחָ֑ד. Tevir (dot plus slant) under the qof of בָּקָ֛ר and the nun of שָׁנָ֛ה. Tipḥa under אֶחָ֖ד and שִׁבְעָ֖ה. Munaḥ under the alef of אַ֣יִל and the pe of פַּ֣ר. Darga under the sin of כְּבָשִׂ֧ים. A silluq stroke under the last mem of תְּמִימִֽם:. The candidate's vowels are unchanged. לַיְיָ between the two parts is deliberately left out; see the remaining questions.
Under the lamed is a T-shaped qamats (bar with a stem), the same shape as the qamats under the first yod. It is not a pair of stacked sheva dots. The shin's own vowel is unchanged.
Three slanting dots under the qof (qubbuts), with no qamats bar. No dagesh is visible in the mem, so none is added.
Under the first mem is a bar with dots beside it (ḥataf pataḥ), wider than the plain two-dot sheva elsewhere on the line. The second mem has a ḥiriq. Recorded as printed, not by grammar.
The mark under the zayin has a descending stem (qamats). The pataḥ under the alef of the same word is a flat bar, which gives a direct comparison.
Pataḥ under the lamed and qamats under the second yod. Nothing is under the first yod. The marks match s270-line19 exactly, which the human read as לַייָ (q399b).

Same Obadiah verse, set in the same type as s270, with the same visible marks: pataḥ under the lamed and qamats under the second yod, with no sheva under the first yod. This matches the human reading for s270 (q399b).
